cohort: 200 pregnant women presenting with antepartum haemorrhage at Patna Medical College and Hospital in Bihar, India.
finding: Placental abruption was associated with significantly worse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including higher rates of preterm delivery, NICU admissions, and perinatal mortality, compared to placenta previa which was linked to caesarean sections and better maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: Caesarean sections were frequently performed in cases of placenta previa, contributing to better maternal outcomes compared to placental abruption.
